detailed_description: StyleGAN is a generative model rather than a classifier. It learns a latent space that can create new samples with similar style and structure, but GAN training is much more sensitive to batch size, learning rate balance, and dataset quality than ordinary supervised models.
beginner_examples: Generating face-like images from a face dataset.
Learning a visual style from an art collection.

hyperparameter_guide.label: Epochs
hyperparameter_guide.brief: Maximum adversarial training epochs.
hyperparameter_guide.lower_values_typically_do: Lower values train faster but may stop before the model has learned enough.
hyperparameter_guide.higher_values_typically_do: Higher values give the model more time to learn, but can overfit or waste time once improvement has flattened.
hyperparameter_guide.example_effect: Example: if validation metrics are still improving at the final epoch, raising this value can help. If validation gets worse while training keeps improving, it is likely too high.

hyperparameter_guide.label: Batch size
hyperparameter_guide.brief: Number of images loaded into each GAN optimization step.
hyperparameter_guide.lower_values_typically_do: Smaller batches use less memory and sometimes generalize better, but updates are noisier.
hyperparameter_guide.higher_values_typically_do: Larger batches give smoother updates and often faster epochs, but need more memory.
hyperparameter_guide.example_effect: Example: 8 or 16 is common on limited hardware, while 32 or 64 is useful when memory allows.

hyperparameter_guide.label: Z latent dimension
hyperparameter_guide.brief: Dimensionality of the random input noise vector.
hyperparameter_guide.lower_values_typically_do: Lower values keep the latent representation smaller and simpler.
hyperparameter_guide.higher_values_typically_do: Higher values allow richer variation but increase model size and training cost.
hyperparameter_guide.example_effect: Example: if StyleGAN is already unstable, increasing latent dimensions is rarely the first fix.

hyperparameter_guide.label: W latent dimension
hyperparameter_guide.brief: Dimensionality of the intermediate latent W space produced by the mapping network.
hyperparameter_guide.lower_values_typically_do: Lower values keep the latent representation smaller and simpler.
hyperparameter_guide.higher_values_typically_do: Higher values allow richer variation but increase model size and training cost.
hyperparameter_guide.example_effect: Example: if StyleGAN is already unstable, increasing latent dimensions is rarely the first fix.

hyperparameter_guide.label: Log2 resolution
hyperparameter_guide.brief: Log2 of the generated output resolution. For example, 7 means 128x128 images.
hyperparameter_guide.lower_values_typically_do: Lower values generate smaller images that are much easier to train.
hyperparameter_guide.higher_values_typically_do: Higher values generate larger, more detailed images but make GAN training much heavier and less stable.
hyperparameter_guide.example_effect: Example: 7 means 128x128 and is far easier to train than 10, which means 1024x1024.

hyperparameter_guide.label: Learning rate
hyperparameter_guide.brief: Generator and mapping-network learning rate.
hyperparameter_guide.lower_values_typically_do: Lower values are safer and more stable, but learning becomes slower.
hyperparameter_guide.higher_values_typically_do: Higher values learn faster but can become unstable or even diverge.
hyperparameter_guide.example_effect: Example: 0.001 is a common safe start for many neural models. If loss jumps around heavily, reduce it.

hyperparameter_guide.label: Optimizer
hyperparameter_guide.brief: Optimizer family used for generator and discriminator training.

options_explained.effect: Adam with StyleGAN-style betas for both generator and discriminator.
RMSProp for both generator and discriminator.

hyperparameter_guide.selection_advice: Adam is usually the easiest beginner start for neural models. SGD is useful when you want explicit momentum-based control. RMSProp and related adaptive optimizers can help on noisy gradients.

hyperparameter_guide.label: Discriminator learning rate
hyperparameter_guide.brief: Learning rate used for the discriminator. If omitted, it falls back to the generator learning rate.
hyperparameter_guide.lower_values_typically_do: Lower values are safer and more stable, but learning becomes slower.
hyperparameter_guide.higher_values_typically_do: Higher values learn faster but can become unstable or even diverge.
hyperparameter_guide.example_effect: Example: 0.001 is a common safe start for many neural models. If loss jumps around heavily, reduce it.

hyperparameter_guide.label: R1 penalty
hyperparameter_guide.brief: Strength of the R1 regularization term applied to real-image gradients.
hyperparameter_guide.lower_values_typically_do: Lower values regularize the discriminator less.
hyperparameter_guide.higher_values_typically_do: Higher values make the discriminator smoother and more constrained, but too much can slow learning.
hyperparameter_guide.example_effect: Example: if GAN training oscillates badly, moderate R1 regularization often helps more than increasing learning rates.

description.description: Runs a StyleGAN-like adversarial training loop for image generation using PyTorch.
Requires an extracted image dataset. Labels are ignored; the model only needs images. The backend trains on GPU when available and falls back to CPU otherwise.
StyleGAN training uses a fixed generator, discriminator, and mapping network implementation rather than a user-built layer editor.

sub_parameters.description: Built from a mapping network, style blocks, progressive upsampling blocks, and ToRGB layers.
Built from EqualizedConv2d blocks plus a minibatch standard-deviation head.
The generated image size is 2**log_resolution. For example, 7 means 128x128 and 10 means 1024x1024.
The backend first loads images from any flat directory structure. If none are found, it falls back to torchvision ImageFolder for class-subfolder layouts.
R1 gradient penalty is applied to real images when r1_penalty is greater than zero.
